Q3'26.headline: Revenue rose 26% to $64.6B, above the $61-64B guide, with ad revenue +26% on impressions +10% and price per ad +14%. GAAP operating income fell 37% to $13.0B (20% margin) because of a $9.9B charge for the August 2026 multi-state attorneys general agreement; excluding it, operating income was $22.9B (+11%) and EPS $7.40. Meta guided Q4'26 revenue to $73-76B, raised FY2026 total expenses to $175-179B to absorb the charge, narrowed capex to $135-145B and announced a non-voting share class distributed as a stock dividend (effectively a 2-for-1 split).

points.text: Zuckerberg said more than 10 million people in the US and Canada set up Muse personal agents in about a month and a half, with about 25% using it on any given day. Shopping is the top use case: more than a quarter of users engage in it, with an average purchase size over $200.

Zuckerberg laid out the Muse business model: free for most people with a transaction fee paid by businesses, plus paid subscriptions for advanced models or extra tokens and business tiers. He said Muse is very compute intensive but Meta expects to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year.

Meta shipped Muse Wonder as its first frontier model, along with Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3, Muse Code, two open-weights models and Muse Voice. Zuckerberg said engagement per person in Meta AI has more than doubled since April and that larger models after Muse Wonder are already in training.

Zuckerberg announced the Meta Enterprise Platform, led by CJ Desai, to sell Muse Wonder and later models through the API, Muse Code and other enterprise services. Li said Meta has 500 million self-identified small businesses using its apps and hopes enterprise becomes a new diversified recurring revenue stream.

Li said the Meta Generative Recommender, rolled out to Facebook Feed retrieval, drove a nearly 2% increase in conversions in targeted segments. GEM expansion lifted app ad conversions 9.6%, and partnership ads grew over 97% YoY to a run rate above $15B.

Li said Instagram time spent per user hit an all-time high with double-digit YoY growth, and Q3 relevance launches lifted Reels time spent by over 4%. Nearly 45% of recommended Instagram Reels are now less than one day old, up more than 11 points from Q2.

Zuckerberg said Meta will ship new VR devices only on major breakthroughs and will focus Reality Labs on personal superintelligence through glasses. He expects the RL operating loss to fall to about $15B in 2027 and trend toward profitability after that. Li guided 2026 RL losses to $18-19B.

Q3 expenses included a $9.9B charge for the August 2026 multi-state attorneys general agreement. The non-deductible part of the charge pushed the tax rate to 24%. Li flagged more youth-related trials scheduled in the US in the coming months.

Meta announced a new class of non-voting stock to be distributed one-for-one to existing shareholders, with trading expected to begin in late January 2027. Li said it is meant for capital raising, employee compensation and acquisitions while preserving the founder-led voting structure, and that there are no specific financing plans yet.

FY2026 total expenses $175-179B (raised from $165-169B to include the $9.9B Q3 legal charge)
FY2026 operating income excluding the Q3 legal charge expected above FY2025

No FY2027 revenue outlook, but Li expects strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027
qa: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley) asked what limits Muse user growth; Zuckerberg said compute efficiency is the main constraint, since Muse has not launched globally because it is compute intensive to run.

Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs) asked about the new share class and capital structure; Li said it creates a publicly traded non-voting stock for capital raising, compensation and M&A, with no specific financing plans to announce.
Doug Anmuth (JPMorgan) asked for a 2027 expense and capex frame; Li said budget and capacity planning is still early and dynamic, and quantitative guidance will come on the Q4 call.

Justin Post (Bank of America) asked whether 2027 revenue growth includes new AI revenue; Li said new AI businesses (subscriptions, transactions, enterprise) can start contributing in 2027 but matter more over time.
Ross Sandler (Barclays) asked about Muse per-user costs; Li gave no figures but cited off-peak capacity, smaller models and inference optimization as efficiency levers.
Mark Mahaney (Evercore ISI) asked whether Muse monetization will come faster than Meta's usual playbook; Zuckerberg said yes, given the size of the costs and the amount of commerce already happening.

Q2'26.headline: Revenue rose 28% (27% constant currency) to $60.8B, at the top of the $58-61B guide, while operating income fell 8% to $18.8B (31% margin) after $2.4B of legal charges and $1.2B of severance from the May 2026 headcount reduction. Excluding those items, operating income would have grown 9%. Meta guided Q3 revenue to $61-64B, raised the low end of FY2026 total expenses to $165-169B, narrowed capex to $130-145B and lifted its tax rate outlook to 15-17%.

points.text: Li introduced Meta Generative Recommender, which uses LLMs to reason about ad content and user preferences together. Combined with GEM and sequence learning, it drove an 8.3% increase in ad clicks and a 15.7% uplift in conversions on Facebook. Advantage+ end-to-end solutions passed a $75B annual run rate.

Zuckerberg said MSL shipped Muse Spark 1.1 and Muse Image, and daily Meta AI users rose 60% since Muse Spark was integrated. Muse Spark 1.1 is available through a new public API, including on OpenRouter for US developers.

Meta Business Agents became available globally on WhatsApp and Messenger, with more than 1 million businesses using them each week, according to Zuckerberg. He described a large enterprise opportunity spanning APIs, business agents and possibly selling compute directly, noting offers for Meta's compute at a significant premium to its cost.

Li said capacity plans are geared toward maximizing 2026 and 2027 capacity, while 2028+ plans keep flexibility by laying down land, power and data center shells ahead of server decisions. Meta also announced a 1GW El Paso data center venture with BlackRock.

Q2 expenses included $2.4B of legal charges and $1.2B of severance tied to the May 2026 headcount reduction affecting about 8,000 employees. Li said that, excluding those items, Q2 operating income would have grown 9%.

Li said Meta shipped its largest single Reels ranking improvement to date, and over half of recommended Instagram Feed content is now less than one day old. Every public Instagram Reels and Feed post is processed by an LLM for content understanding.

qa: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley) asked about 2027 capex; Li gave no outlook but said near-term capacity is more valuable than long-term capacity and planning stays dynamic.

Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs) asked about the debt/equity mix for funding; Li said Meta has added more cost-efficient, long-duration debt and partnerships like BlackRock alongside operating cash flow.

Doug Anmuth (JPMorgan) asked why Meta buys third-party compute while getting offers to sell its own; Zuckerberg said there is nowhere near enough compute for demand and selling it all for short-term profit would be foolish.
Ross Sandler (Barclays) asked about open source; Zuckerberg said Meta will do a mix of open and closed and expects to release open models again soon.

Ken Gawrelski (Wells Fargo) asked if maximizing 2026-27 capacity is a demand or supply statement; Li said both: Meta is demand constrained, including in the core business, and long-term supply is uncertain.

EPS of $10.44 included an $8.03B tax benefit tied to new US Treasury guidance on R&D capitalization ($7.31 without it). Meta guided Q2 revenue to $58-61B, kept FY2026 expenses at $162-169B, raised capex to $125-145B on higher component (memory) prices and announced a May headcount reduction.

points.text: Zuckerberg said Muse Spark, the first model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, made Meta AI a world-class assistant and showed the lab is on track. Li said Meta AI sessions per user rose double digits after the rollout, and more advanced models were already in training.

Meta raised 2026 capex to $125-145B, mainly due to higher component costs, particularly memory pricing. Zuckerberg said Meta is rolling out more than 1GW of custom silicon developed with Broadcom plus significant AMD capacity. Multi-year cloud deals and infrastructure purchases drove a $107B step-up in contractual commitments.

Li said Meta planned to reduce its employee base in May to create a leaner operating model and offset infrastructure investment. She also said that, despite the capex increase, the company still expected 2026 operating income above 2025.

Li said the adaptive ranking model, an LLM-scale ads recommender used at inference, drove a 1.6% increase in conversion rates on major surfaces after expanding to offsite conversions. The Value Optimization Suite passed a $20B run rate (more than doubling) and partnership ads reached a $10B run rate.

Li said ranking improvements lifted Instagram Reels time spent by 10%, and Facebook total video time rose more than 8% globally in Q1, the largest quarter-over-quarter gain in four years. Same-day posts now make up more than 30% of recommended Reels.

Business AI conversations grew to more than 10 million per week, from 1 million at the start of the year, after expanding to Latin America, Indonesia and Asia Pacific. Li said business AIs are free for most businesses today, with monetization to come.

Mark Shmulik (Bernstein) asked about 2027 capex; Li gave no outlook but said Meta has continued to underestimate its compute needs and can slow the ramp if it overbuilds.
Youssef Squali (Truist) asked about the headcount reduction; Li said Meta does not know its optimal future size and is using AI tools to raise productivity while keeping operations efficient.
Doug Anmuth (JPMorgan) asked about Manus; Li said details were still being worked through, so there was no update.
Ron Josey (Citi) asked how much runway is left in ranking improvements; Li said there is still a lot of room, citing longer interaction sequences, retrieval redesign and LLM-based feed controls.

It set FY2026 total expenses at $162-169B and capex at $115-135B, while promising 2026 operating income above 2025.

points.text: Li said the Q1 guide reflects strong demand through the end of Q4 and into early 2026, plus a 4-point FX benefit, 3 points more than in Q4. She clarified that the 2026 promise is operating income above 2025 in absolute dollars, not faster growth.

Li said Meta doubled the GPUs used to train GEM. GEM plus a new sequence learning architecture drove a 3.5% lift in Facebook ad clicks and more than 1% more Instagram conversions. Video generation tools reached a combined $10B revenue run rate.

Instagram Reels watch time rose more than 30% YoY in the US. Facebook Q4 optimizations drove a 7% lift in organic Feed and video views, the largest quarterly revenue impact from Facebook product launches in two years.

Zuckerberg said glasses sales more than tripled in 2025. He expected 2026 Reality Labs losses to be similar to 2025, which would likely be the peak, with most RL investment going to glasses and wearables.

WhatsApp paid messaging passed a $2B annual run rate in Q4. US click-to-message ad revenue grew more than 50% YoY, and business AIs in Mexico and the Philippines reached over 1 million weekly conversations.

Zuckerberg announced Meta Compute and said Dina Powell McCormick will lead partnerships with governments and capital partners. Li said Meta remains capacity constrained through much of 2026 and may eventually carry a positive net debt balance.

Doug Anmuth (JPMorgan) asked about free cash flow and JVs; Li said cash generation supports the 2026 build while Meta explores structures for long-term flexibility.
Justin Post (Bank of America) asked about revenue beyond ads; Zuckerberg said ads will be by far the main growth driver for the next couple of years.

points.text: Zuckerberg said it is the right strategy to aggressively front-load capacity for the most optimistic superintelligence timelines. If those timelines prove too early, the extra compute would accelerate the core business, and in the worst case Meta would slow new builds.

Li said expense growth accelerated 20 points from Q2 because of legal charges, AI talent compensation and infrastructure costs. She expected 2026 expenses to grow at a significantly faster percentage rate than 2025, led by infrastructure (cloud and depreciation).
Zuckerberg said recommendation improvements drove 5% more Facebook time spent in Q3 and 10% more on Threads. Instagram video time was up more than 30% YoY, and Reels passed a $50B annual run rate.
Zuckerberg said revenue running through Meta's fully end-to-end AI-powered ad tools passed a $60B annual run rate. Li said advertisers using Advantage+ lead campaigns see a 14% lower cost per lead.

Zuckerberg said Meta Superintelligence Labs already has the highest talent density in the industry and Meta AI has more than a billion monthly actives. He described the newly launched Vibes as the next generation of Meta's AI creation tools and content experiences.

Li explained that the Blue Owl joint venture for the Louisiana data center moves future construction costs out of capex. Meta contributes 20% of the remaining construction costs, recorded as other investing cash flows.

points.text: Zuckerberg set out the goal of personal superintelligence and created Meta Superintelligence Labs, led by Alexandr Wang, with Nat Friedman on products and applied research and Shengjia Zhao as Chief Scientist. He said the Prometheus cluster comes online in 2026 as the first 1GW+ cluster, and Hyperion can scale to 5GW.
Zuckerberg said the new AI-powered ads recommendation model drove roughly 5% more ad conversions on Instagram and 3% on Facebook after expanding to new surfaces with more signals and longer context.
Zuckerberg said recommendation improvements led to a 5% increase in Facebook time spent and 6% on Instagram in the quarter. Meta AI passed 1 billion monthly actives.

Li said 2026 expense growth will exceed 2025, driven mainly by a sharp acceleration in depreciation and second by compensation for AI talent hired during 2025. G&A fell 27% in Q2 on lower legal costs.

Li warned the European Commission could impose changes to the Less Personalized Ads offering that would significantly hurt European revenue as early as later in Q3. Meta has appealed the DMA decision.

thesis.summary: Meta runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and Threads, used by 3.64B people daily, and earns about 98% of revenue from advertising sold through an AI-driven auction (FY2025 revenue $201.0B, Family of Apps operating income $102.5B). Its edge is scale of engagement plus ranking and ads models (GEM, Andromeda, Lattice, Generative Recommender) that keep lifting time spent and conversions, so revenue growth has accelerated to 22-33% YoY across 2025-26. Management is reinvesting that cash flow in compute and Meta Superintelligence Labs to build frontier Muse models, personal agents (Muse), business agents and an enterprise platform, with FY2026 capex of $135-145B and total expenses of $175-179B. The debate is whether this AI build-out (free cash flow turned negative in Q3'26 and debt reached $83.7B) earns a return beyond the core ads business. Legal costs from youth-related cases and a shrinking but still large Reality Labs loss add to the uncertainty.

pillars.title: AI-driven ads engine still compounding
pillars.text: Ad revenue growth accelerated from 16% in Q1'25 to 33% in Q1'26 and held at 26% in Q3'26. Both volume (impressions) and price per ad grew. Management attributes the gains to larger ranking models, LLM-based retrieval and end-to-end automation, which raise conversions for advertisers.

segments.name: Family of Apps (advertising)
segments.text: Advertising on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and Threads, sold through an automated auction. Q3'26 ad revenue was $63.1B (+26%). FoA operating income was $17.1B, depressed by the $9.9B legal charge (FY2025 $102.5B). Growth comes from impressions (engagement, new surfaces such as Threads and WhatsApp Status) and price per ad (conversion gains).

themes.text: Meta keeps scaling GEM and sequence-learning architectures and is moving to LLM-based generative retrieval for ads and content.
themes.quote: This is the first time we have found a recommendation model architecture that can scale with similar efficiency as LLMs.

themes.text: Management repeatedly ties revenue strength to AI-driven ad performance.
themes.quote: And on a dollar basis, our ads business is reporting faster year-over-year revenue growth than any other company's reported ad business.

themes.text: Spare compute is expected to be put to profitable use in ranking and ads.
themes.quote: If it takes longer, then we'll use the extra compute to accelerate our core business -- which continues to be able to profitably use much more compute than we've been able to throw at it.

segments.name: Family of Apps other revenue (messaging, subscriptions)
segments.text: WhatsApp paid business messaging, Meta Verified and Meta One subscriptions, now the base for business agents and enterprise offerings. It is small ($1.1B in Q3'26) but growing 50-74% YoY.

themes.text: Paid messaging crossed a $2B run rate in Q4'25.
themes.quote: Paid messaging within WhatsApp continues to scale as well, crossing a $2 billion annual run-rate in Q4.

themes.text: Business AIs went from about 1M weekly conversations at the start of 2026 to global availability.
themes.quote: We made Meta Business Agents available globally this quarter on WhatsApp and Messenger, and there are already more than 1 million businesses using them to talk to their customers or complete sales every week.

segments.name: Meta Superintelligence Labs, Muse and enterprise (inside FoA costs)
segments.text: MSL (formed mid-2025) builds the Muse model family (Spark, Wonder, Image, Code, Voice), the Muse personal agent and the Meta Enterprise Platform. It is not a reported segment: its costs sit in Family of Apps and drive most of the capex and expense growth.

themes.text: The stated north star since Q2'25, now productized as Muse.
themes.quote: Meta's vision is to bring personal superintelligence to everyone -- so that people can direct it towards what they value in their own lives.

themes.text: Muse is compute-heavy today, and management targets a sharp drop in serving cost.
themes.quote: In the near term, Muse is very compute intensive to run, but we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale.

themes.text: Management has repeatedly raised capex, arguing it keeps underestimating its compute needs.
themes.quote: Consequently, our current plans are geared towards maximizing 2026 and 2027 capacity.

segments.name: Reality Labs
segments.text: AI glasses (Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta, Meta Ray-Ban Display, Meta-branded glasses), Quest VR and Horizon. Revenue is small ($443M in Q3'26, -6% as Quest declines while glasses grow) and the loss was $19.2B in FY2025. Management is pivoting to glasses with Muse and expects losses to shrink.

themes.text: FY2025 was flagged as the likely peak loss year, and the 2026-27 guides now confirm the decline.
themes.quote: So with these factors combined, we expect that the P&L of Reality Labs to improve from here, with operating loss coming down to around $15 billion next year and trending towards profitability from there.

themes.text: Glasses are management's fastest-growing hardware line.
themes.quote: Sales of our glasses more than tripled last year, and we think that they're some of the fastest growing consumer electronics in history.

risks.text: Youth-safety litigation: $2.4B of legal charges in Q2'26 and a $9.9B charge for the August 2026 multi-state attorneys general agreement in Q3'26, with more US youth-related trials scheduled that management says may result in a material loss.

Capex overbuild and cash burn: FY2026 capex of $135-145B (vs $72.2B in FY2025) turned Q3'26 free cash flow to -$2.1B, debt rose to $83.7B and buybacks stopped in 2026. Returns on GenAI spend are much earlier on the curve than core AI, per the CFO.
Muse and agent unit economics: serving costs are high and rising with users. Monetization (commerce fees, subscriptions) is unproven, and the 10x efficiency gain is a target, not a result.
EU regulation: the European Commission's DMA case on the Less Personalized Ads offering could significantly hurt European revenue. Meta rolled out further LPA changes in Q1'26.

Tax volatility: a $15.93B non-cash charge in Q3'25 from the new US tax law, partly reversed by an $8.03B benefit in Q1'26 after Treasury guidance. The outlook was raised to 15-17% for later 2026 quarters.

Execution and talent: a May 2026 reduction of about 8,000 employees (headcount down 15% YoY) while competing for scarce AI talent, plus dependence on memory and chip supply whose pricing already forced a capex increase.

debates.q: Will the AI capex earn an adequate return?
debates.bull: Core ads already show measurable returns (ad growth of 26-33%), and spare compute can go to ranking, the API or even external sale at a premium.
debates.bear: Spend roughly doubles in 2026 and grows again in 2027. FCF turned negative in Q3'26, and MSL/Muse returns are years out and unquantified.

debates.q: Can Muse become a new profit pool?
debates.bull: 10M+ users in six weeks with 25% daily use, heavy shopping activity (average purchase above $200) and a business model built on commerce fees plus subscriptions.
debates.bear: Muse is US/Canada only, compute intensive, and competes with frontier labs. Monetization depends on businesses accepting agent-driven commerce.

debates.q: Can operating income keep growing through the investment cycle?
debates.bull: Management still guides FY2026 operating income above FY2025 excluding the legal charge, and Q3'26 operating income grew 11% excluding it, with headcount cuts offsetting compensation.
debates.bear: GAAP operating income fell 8% in Q2'26 and 37% in Q3'26, expenses are growing 55-68%, and 2027 depreciation will rise further.

debates.bull: The large attorneys general agreement has been booked and RL losses are shrinking, cleaning up the P&L for 2027.
debates.bear: Management keeps flagging more youth-related trials. EU DMA remedies and the new non-voting share class raise governance and dilution concerns.
